data.text: [00:00]CD1 Track 10
I = Interviewer, T = Tony
[00:03.8]Welcome Tony …
[00:06]Hello. Great to be here.

[00:07.8]So, we know that the James Bond films are incredibly successful ... but as I said, the theme songs are hugely popular too. `[00:17]I mentioned Another Way to Die ... Can you tell us a bit about that one?
[00:22]Yeah, that’s right ... , Another Way to Die is from the film Quantum of Solace. `[00:27]It came out in 2008 ... and was really popular.
[00:30.8]It’s a duet, isn’t it?

[00:32.9]Yes, it’s a duet by Alicia Keys and Jack White – the lead singer of The White Stripes. `[00:37.8]Actually, it’s the first duet used for a Bond theme song – all the others are solos, with just one singer. `[00:44.9]I think it appealed to young people ... although some people didn’t like it at first. `[00:49.7]The words of the song are great ... . Personally I loved it.
[00:53]Yes, the lyrics are really good and have a strong message. `[00:57]And I think Alicia Keys is very cool. `[01:00]I love that song – let’s hear a bit of it ...
[01:51.5]... Mmm ... great song. So, ... when was the first famous Bond theme song?

[01:57.7]Well, the first Bond film, Dr No, and the second one actually, From Russia with Love ... had great soundtracks. `[02:05]They had music, obviously. `[02:06.9]But they didn’t have a theme song connected with them. Goldfinger was the first big song.
[02:12]Mmmm. That’s right ... Goldfinger ... .
[02:14]When Goldfinger came out, in 1964, the real connection between film and theme song started. `[02:21.8]After that, I suppose the public expected a great theme song in every film.
[02:26]Yes, that was a great film. `[02:28.2]And Shirley Bassey made Goldfinger into a classic song, too.
[02:32.6]Yes, she’s an amazing singer. `[02:35]That song started her career and she became an international star immediately. `[02:40.9]It wasn’t Bassey’s only Bond song, either.
[02:43.7]Oh, yes. That’s true... How many did she sing?
[02:47]She sang three Bond songs altogether – the only singer to do more than one.
[02:51.8]Really?

[02:52.7]Yes, she sang another classic song, Diamonds are Forever, in 1971. `[02:58.2]And then eight years later, Moonraker, although that one wasn’t very successful. `[03:03.9]But it’s not just Shirley Bassey. `[03:05.9]What’s good about Bond is that there are different singers and different styles for each film. `[03:10.9]Many of the songs really are classics ... .
[03:13.5]Tell us about some of the other successful ones ...

[03:16.3]Well, yes, many Bond songs got to the top of the charts in different countries ... but A View to a Kill by Duran Duran is the only Bond song actually to be Number One on the Billboard Hot 100 chart ... .
[03:30.3]The only Number One ... ? A View to a Kill ...? Really? That’s interesting.

[03:35.5]Mmm ... there are other real classics which did really well. `[03:39.5]In the 1970s, there were two great Bond songs. `[03:44]First Live and Let Die, by Paul McCartney and Wings in 1973. `[03:49.2]Then, Nobody Does it Better by Carly Simon in 1977.
[03:54]And Another Way to Die of course that we talked about earlier ... Jack White and Alicia Keys had huge success with that one.
[04:02]Yes, that was one of my personal favourites ...
[04:04.7]Not all Bond songs were hits though, were they? `[04:08.2]There have been some flops too.

[04:10.6]Yes, there was a very mixed reaction to Madonna’s Die Another Day, when it came out in 2002. `[04:17.7]It wasn’t a complete flop ... but strangely, it got awards for being the best song, but also the worst!
[04:25.4]I liked that one actually ... I thought it had a really catchy chorus.
[04:30.5]Did you? Yes, I thought so, too.
